title: NEW SEKA Exaero GR Build With the Chainbox Pro Mechanic

takeaways.text: The first frame had an unspecified fault, so the mechanic declined to build it; SEKA shipped a replacement from China in just under a week.

The mechanic found the build smooth apart from routing hoses through the one-piece bar; he praised the channelled fork routing, flat-faced brake mounts, T47 threads that ran in by hand and a clean frame interior.
Split clip-off headset spacers let the stem height change without disconnecting the hoses; the long seatpost must be cut because insertion is limited.
A 50 mm rear tire on Zipp 303 XPLR S wheels was close but cleared; the front Thunder Burt had plenty of room.
With this crankset the chainring sat only about 2 mm from the chainstay; the mechanic put that down to the chosen crank offset, not the frame.

disclosure: UK rider's build video with his mechanic; how the frameset was obtained and any sponsorship are not stated.
summary: UK shop build of a SEKA ExAero GR after a faulty first frame was replaced, with the mechanic's assessment of finish, routing and clearance.
